description.narrative: Insatsens övergripande mål är att adressera utmaningar och behov relaterade till tillgång till identitetshandlingar (civil dokumentation) och rättigheter gällande bostad, mark och egendom (HLP ¬ Housing, land and property) för återvändare, internflyktingar, inklusive återvändare från nordöstra Syrien, miljömigranter och värdsamhällen.

The overall objective of the intervention is to address challenges and needs related to access to identity documents (civil documentation) and rights concerning housing, land and property (HLP) for returnees, internally displaced persons — including returnees from northeast Syria — environmental migrants, and host communities

The project aims to support the return and reintegration of displaced populations by addressing key barriers that hinder their ability to rebuild their lives. It will promote durable solutions and facilitate the social and economic reintegration of internally displaced persons (IDPs), including those displaced due to climate change, IDP returnees, returnees from Northeast Syria (NES) and returnees from abroad, as well as host communities through facilitating their access to civil documentation and housing, land and property (HLP) rights, and enhancing their active engagement in community.
This will be achieved through (1) providing direct assistance, (2) supporting the government in addressing structural obstacles through strengthening the systems and institutions overseeing issuance of civil documentation, and (3) building and reinforcing the capacities of local entities to foster sustainable reintegration

title.narrative: Signed Agreement IOM Iraq Civil documentation
Beslut om insats (Decision of agreement IOM civil documentation Iraq 2024-2026)

description.narrative:
Outcome 1: IDPs, returnees, environmental migrants, and host communities are provided with direct legal assistance and are better equipped to rebuild their lives after displacement.
Under this Outcome, IOM provided direct legal assistance to 704 individuals (237 women, 361 men, 50 boys, 56 girls), including displaced populations, returnees, climate induced internally displaced persons, migrants and host communities in Basra, Thiqar and Najaf in the south, and Anbar and Ninewa in the north.. Through individual legal counselling, representation before courts and relevant government institutions and support in navigating complex legal and administrative processes, individuals have obtained documentation, enabling them to rebuild their lives with greater stability and access to essential services, including healthcare, education and social protection. In addition, 710 individuals (193 women, 501 men, 9 boys, 7 girls) have benefited from legal information and awareness raising sessions, strengthening their understanding of their legal rights and how to enjoy them. To achieve this, IOM has collaborated with the local authorities and the relevant government institutions responsible for issuance of documentation, including the Ministry of Health represented by the Directorate of Health, the Ministry of Interior (MoI) represented by the Directorate of Civil Affairs and the Ministry of Justice represented by the relevant courts.
Moreover, IOM case management services strengthened access to protection services for at least 30 individuals (including 6 with disabilities) who experienced forced eviction or destruction of personal property, psychological/emotional abuse or inflicted distress, as well as gender based violence, including denial of resources, physical assault and psychological abuse. These individuals were located in AlManathera, Najaf, and Kufa districts (Najaf governorate). Through external referrals, IOM improved access to specialized support for persons with special needs. Complementing individualized protection support, 49 community awareness raising sessions were held in AlManathera, Najaf, and Kufa districts (Najaf governorate). These sessions aimed to improve community understanding of early marriage, gender based violence, human rights and protection. These sessions increased participants awareness and prevention capacity.
Additionally, capacity building training provided to 11 civil society organizations (CSOs) throughout 2025 further increased local actors knowledge of protection risks and strengthened their capacity to identify cases and conduct necessary referrals. IOM is undertaking a gender analysis in the Najaf area, examining gender dynamics within climate affected households and the broader local community using focus group discussions and key informant interviews with climate affected households, host community members, and a range of local stakeholders. The results will be shared with local/municipality authority representatives, local leaders, health service providers, as well as local CSOs working in this area.
Through this work, populations experiencing displacement or migration have gained practical access to their legal rights, improved knowledge of their entitlements and the ability to seek protection support and address documentation challenges. As a result, individuals have become less vulnerable to marginalization, exploitation and engagement in harmful coping strategies, including irregular migration or involvement in extremists' networks. With this recognition and support, targeted populations have increased their trust in their communities and their government, fostering greater social cohesion and empowerment.
Early engagement with communities, combined with context sensitive awareness and protection and legal support, have made the delivery of services accessible and meaningful for everyone. Moreover, the collaborative approach with local actors, including local authorities and civil society organizations, has demonstrated its impact on sustainability of interventions. As a result, IOM will strengthen its community based approach during the upcoming period, ensuring that working within a framework that promotes community engagement and leadership.
Outcome 2: Government counterparts are engaged to lift structural obstacles hindering populations access to documentation and HLP rights and the systems and institutions in charge of the processing and issuance of documentation are strengthened.
Under this Outcome, IOM has maintained a strong focus on systemic change, engaging with relevant counterparts and government institutions to address structural obstacles that limit access to documentation and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) rights. By working collaboratively with other UN agencies, such as the UN HABITAT, and government counterparts, such as the Ministry of Migration and Displaced (MoMD) and the MoI through meetings and consultations, IOM has laid out the groundwork for the implementation of strategic workshops and capacity building and development activities in the upcoming quarter. This will strengthen the government's capacity and facilitate issuance of documentation for targeted populations, especially those affected by climate change.
Furthermore, IOM has supported 15 relevant government institutions with in kind support in response to their specific needs, contributing to improved operational readiness and service delivery. As a result, government counterparts are increasingly aware of both their technical capacities and the systemic constraints they face, and are becoming more responsive to the needs of displaced populations and returnees. This work supports longer term institutional reform and helps ensure that gains achieved through direct assistance are sustained over time.
Despite this progress, several structural challenges continue to affect access to documentation and HLP rights. These include limited coordination between local and national authorities, inconsistencies in procedures and requirements across institutions, and variation in practices between governorates, which can create confusion and unequal access for affected populations. High staff turnover within government institutions further affects continuity and institutional memory, while the lack of standardized procedures across governorates continues to pose challenges for individuals navigating administrative systems.
In terms of lessons learnt so far into implementation, IOM has realized that government engagement is most effective when accompanied by dialogue and evidence from field level interventions and tailored technical support, and this is the approach that will be followed for the upcoming period.
Outcome 3: Conditions for sustainable returns and reintegration (focusing on IDPs, IDP returnees, returnees from abroad, environmental migrants, and host communities) are enhanced through strengthening local capacities and structures in areas of return. IOM has initiated preparations for the implementation of activities under this Outcome. Efforts will focus on preparing individuals and communities for safe, dignified and sustainable returns, through engagement with local actors and CSOs.
IOMs experience on localization has demonstrated that the most successful reintegration takes place when communities are actively involved in planning and implementation, and when initiatives are inclusive of multiple stakeholders, including local authorities and actors, as well as CSOs. This community led approach will promote local ownership, which is crucial for sustainable reintegration and social cohesion.
